newsitem.title: UK: IBCA - EMU positive or neutral for member ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA - EMU positive or neutral for member ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agnecy, said on Thursday that European Economic and Monetary (EMU) would be positive or neutral for participating countries.
But IBCA added that governments involved in EMU would not automatically be rated AAA.

"Most EU countries would make substantial savings in the interest payments on their national debt as a result of the likely fall in bond yields which will occur for EMU participants," IBCA said in a report.
It said these gains would be particularly large for Spain, Portugal and Italy -- ranging from 2.5 percent to nearly 6.00 percent of GDP.
"Even Britain could eventually benefit by some 0.7 percent of GDP, worth more than two pence (per pound) off the basic rate of income tax," IBCA said.
IBCA said that even though participating governments will have the power to tax in euros, they will lose their power to print money, and would not automatically be rated AAA.

"The ratings will therefore be more like their foreign currency rating of the likely participants -- AA plus for Belgium and Ireland, and AA for Finland -- then their local currency ratings -- AAA in the case of all likely participants," IBCA said.
"However, there may be changes in individual countries' ratings depending on the particular impact of EMU."

The credit rating agency said that although small, peripheral European countries were more vulnerable to economic shocks, they also had more flexible labour markets, meaning that the loss of the exchange rate as a means of adjustment was less serious.

"Given the other benefits -- notably substantial savings in foreign exchange transaction costs which are proportionately higher for small countries, and a likely investment increase -- the rating implications would be positive or neutral," IBCA said.

It added that the independence of the European System of Central Banks would also reduce the likelihood of macro-economic policy instability and create a low inflation and low interest rate environment for European business.
